title: Thoracic cage (anterior)

rows: Upper part of the sternum, at the level of the T3 and T4 vertebrae.
Both clavicles, the first costal cartilages, the upper half of the second costal cartilages, and the body of the sternum.
Jugular (suprasternal) notch on its upper border, with a clavicular notch on each side.
hy: It meets the body at the sternal angle (angle of Louis), which marks the second costal cartilage and lies at the level of the disc between T4 and T5. At this level the arch of the aorta begins and ends and the trachea divides.

rows: Longest part of the sternum, between the manubrium and the xiphoid process, at the level of the T5 to T9 vertebrae.
Manubrium above, the xiphoid process below, and the costal cartilages of the second to seventh ribs on each side.
Transverse ridges mark where its four segments fused.
Small lower end of the sternum, at about the level of the T10 vertebra.
Made of cartilage in the young. It turns to bone in adult life. The diaphragm and rectus abdominis attach to it.
The upper seven pairs of ribs.
Each joins the sternum through its own costal cartilage, so they are also called vertebrosternal ribs.

The eighth, ninth, and tenth pairs of ribs.
Their costal cartilages do not reach the sternum. Each joins the cartilage of the rib above, and together they form the costal margin. Ribs 11 and 12 are also counted as false ribs.

The lowest two pairs of ribs.
